new_statements.quote: Fungwa has two contrastive tones, namely H(igh) and L(ow). H tone is marked with an acute accent ([bé] 'that'), and L tone is marked with a grave accent ([kà] 'you'). [...] The attested syllable patterns in Fungwa can be summarised as (C)V(V) or N. The syllables may not have a coda but may generally bear an onset. The core of the syllable in Fungwa is either a vowel or a syllabic nasal. The language has two tones with the mora as its tone-bearing unit.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Fungwa is described as a two-tone (H/L) language with the mora as tone-bearing unit; all four accessible descriptions (Akinbo 2019, 2021 diss., 2021 Phonology, 2023 PDA) treat word prosody exclusively in terms of tone and make no statement about word stress, accent, or metrical feet (the dissertation explicitly omits the foot from Fungwa prosodic structure as irrelevant, p. 135). No stress placement rule exists in the literature opened.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress statement). Tonal notes: L-H not attested on a single bimoraic syllable; final lowering of H at the end of an intonational phrase (§5.4.1, p. 173ff.).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone (mora as TBU); final lowering is stated at the intonational-phrase edge. Citation forms are phonetically transcribed elicited nouns and short sentences from six Fungwa villages (Rafi LGA, Niger State), elicited 2015-2018.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources describe Cifungwa/Fungwa (ISO ula) as spoken in six villages of Rafi LGA, Niger State, Nigeria (c. 1000 speakers), i.e. the language-level fung1245; no dialect distinction is drawn. Older names Ura/Ula refer to the same language.

[...] The attested syllable patterns in Fungwa can be summarised as (C)V(V) or N. The syllables may not have a coda but may generally bear an onset. sources.locator: §2.6 Tone, p. 41 (pdf p. 60) and §2.7 Summary, p. 45 (pdf p. 64)
sources.note: Silent on word stress. Ch. 2 'Introduction to Fungwa phonology' (§2.2 syllable structure, §2.6 Tone pp. 41-45) describes two contrastive tones H and L with the mora as TBU; the only occurrences of 'stress' are cross-linguistic (Kobon, pp. 204-205, used as an analogy for prominence-based licensing). The foot is deliberately left out of the prosodic structure as 'not relevant' (p. 135). No pitch-accent, prominence or intonation-based word-stress statement anywhere; §5.4.1 treats final lowering at the intonational-phrase edge (p. 173ff.).

sources.citation: Akinbo, Samuel Kayode. 2023. Reduplication, repetition and sound symbolism in Fungwa. Phonological Data and Analysis 5(2): 1-24. DOI 10.3765/pda.v5art2.72.
sources.note: p. 3: 'Fungwa contrasts two tones, H(igh) [bá] that and L(ow) [bà] you.' Prosodic word adopted as harmony domain; 'The constituents of ω, namely Foot (F) and Mora (µ), are not relevant to this work' (p. 3-4). No stress statement.
